newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul court upholds sentence on Daewoo chairman.
newsitem.headline: Seoul court upholds sentence on Daewoo chairman.

text.p: South Korea's Supreme Court on Thursday upheld a two year suspended jail sentence for bribery imposed on Kim Woo-choong, founder of the giant Daewoo Group, court officials said.

The court also confirmed a 2-1/2 year suspended jail term on Choi Won-suk, chairman of the Dong Ah Group, another leading conglomerate. Both men were convicted of bribing former president Roh Tae-woo.
Kim's sentence was suspended for three years and Choi's for four years by a lower appeals court in December. The two had appealed against their sentences to the Supreme Court.

The Supreme Court, South Korea's court of final appeal, rejected a prosecution appeal against the acquittal of Chung Tae-soo, the founder of the troubled Hanbo Group, who also had been charged with bribing Roh.
Chung is standing trial on separate charges of bribery in connection with the collapse in January of the group's steelmaking flagship in a loans scandal.
The court also confirmed the acquittal of Lee Kyung-hoon, former president of Daewoo Corp. Prosecutors had challenged the acquittal of Lee by the lower court.
